instructions: Edit this file to update every measured figure on the site. Do not add a number unless it is in the resume or in a committed result file in the project's repository. The home page, case studies, and tables all read from here. Each project has one headline stat (headline.stat), three short facts (factIds), and a short caveat. Search this file for the old value and update every place it appears, including caveat text.

projects.title: Time-series foundation model
projects.summary: A decoder-only transformer pretrained from scratch in PyTorch, then scored zero-shot on datasets held out of training after overlapping benchmark series were removed.
projects.caveat: The 0.605× is a validation result, and the 10.1M-parameter patch_s2 checkpoint has no test score. A smaller CPU model (833,440 parameters, 3 seeds, 97 configurations) was scored once on the test split: CRPS 1.109× Seasonal Naive, no detectable difference, and 1.217× AutoARIMA, worse.

projects.title: World Shock Lab
projects.summary: Event studies of Federal Reserve, Bank of Canada, and OPEC surprises across global assets, with a pre-registered test of whether machine learning adds anything, and a scenario tool published before each decision.
projects.caveat: Machine learning did not beat the linear model on the average move in either pre-registered study. Quantile boosting won only on 5% tail pinball loss. None of 80 regime tests survived false-discovery control.

image.alt: World Shock Lab scenario for a Federal Reserve hike and an oil supply cut, with bands around six Canadian assets.

tsxFed.label: TSX move on a 10 bp Fed surprise
tsxFed.source: world-shock-lab README headline findings and docs/RESULTS.md: S&P/TSX −1.10% on the day of a Fed move scaled to a 10 bp rise in the US 2-year (90% band −1.59 to −0.61). Resume: −1.10%.

tsxBoc.label: Same-size Bank of Canada surprise
tsxBoc.source: world-shock-lab README: −0.19% after a BoC move of the same size (90% band −0.33 to −0.04), or −0.75% with Rigobon–Sack. Resume: −0.19%.

projects.title: Orbit
projects.summary: Autonomous Incident Commander is a scripted demo on a fictional e-commerce corpus: the team counts errors in code, checks runbook thresholds, finds the bad deploy, and the auditor refuses a red-team agent's fake root cause. The measured results are still the frozen makerspace test, a local planner, worker and critic. The six-role team has not been scored.
projects.caveat: Measured once on a frozen 12-task test (3 agents, harness v2). Task success went from 2 to 3 of 12, and that gain is not significant: the paired interval includes zero. The harness has since changed to v3, and the rescore under v3 is pending. The six-role v2 team has not been scored.

projects.title: ATLAS
projects.purpose: An economic research terminal that traces how a cost shock travels through the world's production networks.
projects.summary: Real country data, seven OECD production tables, a PyTorch scenario solver and saved neural checkpoints, served by one local FastAPI process with a React interface. Every result is labelled as observed, hypothetical or learned.
projects.caveat: A local research terminal, not a hosted service. In the graph experiment, ridge regression beat every neural and graph model on the one held-out year. Latencies are warm requests on one machine.

image.alt: ATLAS World Atlas view: a map of real GDP growth by country, with Japan selected and its 2025 figures beside the map.
